subject: Adaptive tier pathway and combo-pricing options for Clipper Health
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clipperhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <m.reed@clipperhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options — compact start, upgrade path, and credits

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We like Redwood’s latency profile but need help translating product packaging into a predictable procurement path for the board. A few questions we need you to confirm before we take this to procurement: 

- Can Clipper start on the Compact plan (metered) and then flip to a Dedicated reserve without a full reprovisioning penalty? Does Redwood offer an upgrade credit or prorated conversion?
- If we add the realtime-embeddings addon later, will you grandfather our initial commit price or reprice based on new usage?
- What are typical discounts at 6-month and 12-month committed throughput commitments (we’re looking at an initial pilot ~100k tokens/day then scale)?

We also have security and contract questions — I’ll attach our standard MSA in a separate email. For pricing purposes can you send a short one-pager with 2-3 recommended paths (fastest time-to-value, lowest unit cost, and predictable enterprise path) and a sample conversion math for prorated credits?

Appreciate a concise breakdown—our procurement deadline is EOD next Thursday.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Director, AI Product
Clipper Health

Attachments: (none)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clipperhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — compact start, upgrade path, and credits

Emily — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers up front, then a short set of options attached as a one-pager (Clipper-Proposal-v3.pdf):

TL;DR
- Yes: you can pilot on Compact (metered) and convert to Dedicated with a prorated credit for unused metered spend applied toward the Dedicated commit.
- Addons: existing commit pricing is preserved for previously purchased units; new addons are priced on top but we offer bundling credits when consolidated within 30 days of conversion.
- Discounts: typical ranges are 10%–18% for a 6-month commit and 18%–30% for a 12-month commit depending on throughput and whether you include a reserved GPU pool (Dedicated).

Options (see attached one-pager for numbers):
1) Fast time-to-value (Pilot -> Metered Compact)
   - Start: Compact (metered), no commit.
   - Transition: Convert to Dedicated within 90 days; apply prorated credit equal to remaining metered spend * 0.9 toward commit.
2) Cost-first (6–12 month commit)
   - Start: 6-month commit for baseline throughput (~100k tokens/day). 12-month gives deeper discount and reduced overage rate.
3) Predictable Enterprise (Dedicated + Addons)
   - Reserved GPU pool + SLOs + extended retention. Bundling credit for realtime-embeddings if purchased within conversion window.

We’ve attached MSA redline guidance in the related links and flagged a few typical procurement asks. Marissa has flagged the technical constraints for live embeddings warmup — Marissa, can you add a note on warmup/throughput behavior and recommended buffer?

I’ll follow up with a simple conversion-table that shows example math for a $/1M token basis so procurement can see the delta.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Clipper-Proposal-v3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clipperhealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — compact start, upgrade path, and credits

Emily — quick technical note to help procurement size the commit: 

- Warmup: moving from metered to Dedicated requires a KV cache warmup window; expect a transient 5–15% higher token cost (small) during the first 48–72 hours as we populate caches. We can mitigate with prewarming if you provide a warmup corpus (we charge at metered rates for warmup traffic).
- Addons (realtime-embeddings): embeddings run faster on Dedicated (lower per-embedding unit cost) — our bundling credit assumes you convert within 30 days; otherwise it's evaluated as new spend.
- Proration example (simple): if you’ve spent $24k on Compact in month 1 and convert to a $100k Dedicated commit in month 2, we apply $24k * 0.9 = $21.6k credit to the commit, then invoice the remaining commit balance on your normal schedule.

If you want, we can provide a short CSV with line-by-line math for the procurement team.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@clipperhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options — compact start, upgrade path, and credits

Thanks Markus and Marissa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups before we route to procurement: 

- Can you produce the CSV with the prorated conversion math and a clear example for 100k tokens/day scaling to 500k tokens/day on a 12-month commit? (We want to show the board the cost curve.)
- Please add a line that explicitly states any fees or penalties for early termination after conversion.
- I uploaded our MSA redlines — can Redwood accept the security carve (section 7.2) and the data residency clause we added? I saw the DocuSign link in your related links but would prefer a one-page summary of redlines you can accept/ask to counter.

If you can get the CSV + redline summary by Monday EOD (Aug 23) we’ll circle back to procurement that day. Otherwise we’ll ask for an extension.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emily
